name: Candyman
description: Candyman (also known as Drug Dealer) is a social deduction game using playing cards to assign secret roles. The Candyman tries to secretly wink at Buyers to sell 'candy' while the Cop tries to identify and bust the Candyman before all deals are made.

overview.description: Candyman (also known as Drug Dealer) is a social deduction game using playing cards to assign secret roles. The Candyman tries to secretly wink at Buyers to sell 'candy' while the Cop tries to identify and bust the Candyman before all deals are made.

history.origins: Candyman (also known as Drug Dealer) is a modern social deduction party game that uses playing cards to assign secret roles. The game was documented by Bonnie Fishell and has become popular as a party game due to its simple rules and social interaction elements.
timeline: 20th century: Game created as social party game
Documented by Bonnie Fishell with scoring system
history.cultural: Known by two names - Candyman (family-friendly) and Drug Dealer (adult). The game is popular at parties and gatherings due to its social interaction and bluffing elements.
history.evolution: Originally played without scoring as a casual party game. Bonnie Fishell's version added a scoring system that reflects each role's objectives, making it suitable for competitive play over multiple rounds.

setup.players: 4+ players (best with 6-10). No partnerships - each player has individual objectives based on their secret role.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack using only: 1 Ace (Candyman), 1 King (Cop), and numeral cards (2-10) equal to remaining player count. Total cards = number of players.
setup.dealing: Shuffle the selected cards (1 Ace, 1 King, numeral cards for remaining players). Each player draws one card and looks at it secretly. Do not reveal cards to other players. Ace = Candyman, King = Cop, Numeral = Buyer.
setup.equipment: Standard deck of cards, score sheet for tracking points across rounds

rules.objective: Candyman: Sell candy to as many Buyers as possible without being caught. Buyers: Successfully buy candy by receiving a wink from the Candyman. Cop: Identify and expose the Candyman before all Buyers complete their purchases.
rules.gameplay: All players look around at each other. The Candyman secretly winks at Buyers to make deals. When a Buyer is winked at, they reveal their card, say 'Sold!' (or 'The deal has been made!'), and retire from the round. They must NOT reveal who the Candyman is. The Cop watches for who is winking. When the Cop thinks they know who the Candyman is, they say 'busted' and point at the accused. The accused reveals their card. If correct (Ace), round ends. If wrong (Buyer), round continues - but now everyone knows who the Cop is. Alternative signals: If winking is difficult, players can agree on another signal like tapping the face.
keyRules: Only the Candyman can wink (or use agreed signal)
Buyers who complete a deal reveal their card and retire
Buyers must NOT reveal who the Candyman is
Cop can make multiple accusations but loses points for wrong ones
After first wrong accusation, everyone knows who the Cop is
Round ends when Candyman is busted OR all Buyers have bought

strategy.basic: Candyman: Make eye contact and wink when the Cop isn't looking. Vary your timing. Buyers: Watch everyone carefully to spot who is winking. Cop: Observe facial expressions and eye movements to catch the wink.
strategy.intermediate: Candyman: Use misdirection by looking at multiple people. Time your winks when the Cop is focused elsewhere. Buyers: Notice who other Buyers are watching. Cop: Watch for subtle reactions from Buyers who received winks.
strategy.advanced: Candyman: Establish patterns then break them. Use the Cop's known identity (after wrong accusation) to your advantage. Buyers: Coordinate observations without revealing information. Cop: Use process of elimination and behavioral tells.
tips: Candyman: Don't wink too quickly or too obviously
Buyers: If you get a wink, reveal immediately - waiting helps the Cop
Cop: One wrong accusation makes your job much harder
Alternative signals work better in some lighting conditions
Watch for suppressed smiles from successful Buyers

scoring.description: Points per role: Candyman for sales, Buyers for buying, Cop for correct bust. Wrong bust loses Cop points.
scoring.winCondition: After multiple rounds, highest total score wins. Role objectives: Candyman sell, Buyers buy, Cop bust Candyman.

synthesis.shortDescription: Social deduction party game: one Candyman, one Cop, rest Buyers. Candyman secretly winks at Buyers; Cop tries to bust the Candyman.
